title: Lost a python? Boston Animal Care and Control might have it.
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: A ball python named 'Tippy' was found near Ellington Street in Dorchester by Boston Animal Care and Control.
City officials are seeking the python's owner and have encouraged contact via 617-635-1800 or [email protected].
The discovery was announced among common pet reports, as the agency frequently shares found animal notices on social media.

title: Tommy DeVito bests Drake Maye, and other takeaways from Patriots’ training camp scrimmage
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Tommy DeVito led Team Blue to a 22-15 victory over Team White in the Patriots' training camp scrimmage.
DeMario Douglas excelled for Team Blue, catching six passes and scoring two touchdowns, including a 50-yard reception.
Several key players missed the scrimmage, with Will Campbell expected back soon and Carlton Davis sidelined until next week.

title: A closer look at Harwich, voted the best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich was voted the best town on Cape Cod by over 850 Boston.com readers in an informal poll.
The Lower Cape town offers nearly 11 miles of shoreline, seven villages, and more than 20 beaches.
Local highlights include Saquatucket Marina, The Port Restaurant & Bar, and the Cape Cod Lavender Farm.

title: DA’s office says prosecutor’s ‘hot mic’ moment in Lindsay Clancy trial was misheard
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Plymouth DA's office says a 'hot mic' comment was misheard as 'shut it off,' not 'shut her up'.
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington accused prosecutors of inappropriate comments during Lindsay Clancy's trial.
Judge William Sullivan warned against inappropriate courtroom comments, emphasizing possible ejection without warnings.

title: Little boy dancing to DJ on Boston Common has hundreds of thousands of new fans
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: 4-year-old Chukwuemeka Ikesinachi-Nwogwugwu danced to a DJ's music at Boston Common, gaining viral fame.
His mom filmed and shared the video, which received over 200,000 likes and 4,000 comments online.
The DJ, Miss S. Peace, and onlooker Kelly Werme encouraged his dancing, highlighting Boston's welcoming spirit.

title: Boston wine bar will keep its signature pours, just without the wine
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Barcelona Wine Bar in Boston will serve nonalcoholic porrón drinks due to a three-day liquor license suspension.
The license suspension follows incidents of serving alcohol to underage patrons during a May inspection at the South End location.
Barcelona Wine Bar updated its ID policy, ordering more scanners and enhancing verification protocols after internal investigations.

title: Could Mike Vrabel keep 7 wide receivers on Patriots’ roster?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Patriots have seven wide receivers in contention for the roster, including A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs.
Mike Vrabel is open to starting the season with seven wideouts, prioritizing players who contribute to winning.
Kayshon Boutte and Kyle Williams face roster uncertainty, with Boutte involved in trade rumors and Williams needing to secure a role.

title: Suffolk DA candidates dispute ethics, transparency, experience at Roxbury debate
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Suffolk DA candidates Hayden, Rollins, and Champion clashed over ethics, transparency, and experience at the Roxbury debate.
Both Hayden and Rollins faced scrutiny over past ethics controversies, while Champion positioned herself as the steady alternative.
Candidates differed on transparency in police misconduct investigations, with Rollins advocating for immediate footage release and Hayden urging caution.

title: What Boston meteorologists are saying about this weekend’s humidity levels, the potential for pop-up storms
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: Heat and humidity will persist in southern New England, with a slight ease expected over the weekend.
Pop-up showers and thunderstorms are possible Friday evening and again on Saturday evening.
Sunday is forecasted to remain dry but humid, with temperatures feeling sticky due to dew points in the 60s.

title: Here’s some background behind the vintage baseball glove a Red Sox fan gave to Aroldis Chapman
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Red Sox closer Aroldis Chapman received a vintage 1930s Bob Feller model glove from fan Andy Zides during a game.
The gift coincided with Chapman surrendering a two-run home run, his first earned runs in over a month.
The Red Sox ultimately defeated the White Sox 12-11 in 13 innings, marking their eighth straight victory.
